va:
The letter 'va' is:
- 37th among all letters
- 29th among 33 consonants
- A dantaṭṭhaja (dental-labial) letter among 6 classes of consonants
- Belongs to a-group letters
- 4th in the a-group of 8 letters
- A ghosa (voiced) consonant
- Produced at its own position (sakaṭhāna)
- Pronounced with slight contact between teeth and lips (īsaṃphuṭṭha)
- A parasaya consonant (depending on following vowel)
In Koṭṭhubha, it"s described as:
- The 29th consonant
- A modification of "u"
- Called antaṭṭha and addhaṭṭha
- Termed dantaṭṭhaja due to dental-labial articulation
- Called īsaṃphuṭṭha due to its pronunciation method
Three main types:
1. Ekakkhara (single letter)
2. Suddha (pure/independent)
3. Saṃyogavanta (combined with 13 other consonants like ka, sa, ha)
Grammatical functions:
- Can occur in sandhi combinations
- Functions as nominal, taddhita, and kita suffixes
- Appears in roots: vā, vī, vu, ve, vhe
- Can transform into "ba" in certain positions
Special uses:
- As a particle (nipāta)
- In various root modifications
- In compound formations
- As a substitute for certain vowels in specific contexts
Meanings when used as a noun:
- Mind (neuter)
- Wind (masculine)
- Elephant (masculine)
